request.query: SOME/IP header byte size, Ethernet MTU 1500, IP/UDP overhead, SOME/IP-TP segmentation payload threshold for UDP

evidence.claim_text: The SOME/IP header Length field counts the bytes from the beginning of the Request ID to the end of the message. The total message length is Length + 8. For a basic message without additional headers, Length is 8 plus the payload byte count, and the total size is 16 plus the payload byte count.

evidence.claim_text: All non-final TP segment-data lengths shall be multiples of 16 bytes. This counts segment payload bytes, excluding the SOME/IP and TP headers. A correctly aligned maximum segment-data length of 1392 bytes is recommended, not an unconditional maximum for every deployment.

evidence.claim_text: Senders shall segment only messages configured for segmentation and send segments in ascending order. Non-final segments shall have equal sizes, and the sender shall try to maximize segment size within specification limits.

evidence.claim_text: Each TP segment sets the Message Type TP flag and inserts a four-byte big-endian TP header immediately after the SOME/IP header. From high to low bits it contains a 28-bit Offset, three reserved bits and one More Segments bit.

project_inputs: Transport and IP family, serialized size, header overhead, TP support, reassembly limits, path constraints and actual PMTU mechanism.
expert_knowledge.summary: Separate serialization size, SOME/IP-TP segmentation, IP fragmentation and path-MTU limits.
expert_knowledge.rationale: Each layer has different headers, limits and failure observations; successful small traffic does not identify the failing layer.
alternatives: Use an explicitly bounded message size consistent with the selected path and protocol.
Use supported segmentation or another transport after reviewing semantics; DPLPMTUD is conditional and not mandatory for SOME/IP.
failure_modes: Payload size is confused with full IP packet size.
SOME/IP-TP is mistaken for IP fragmentation.
Probe loss due to congestion is diagnosed as certain MTU failure.
A sender API success is treated as remote reception.
srs_guidance: Define size limits at named layer boundaries and oversize behavior.
Specify only implemented discovery/segmentation capabilities and keep budgets configurable.

preconditions: Transport and IP family, serialized size, header overhead, TP support, reassembly limits, path constraints and actual PMTU mechanism.
stimulus: Sweep sizes around configured boundaries; vary path MTU and PTB visibility in an isolated test; separately vary TP reassembly capacity.
observations: Capture serialized and wire sizes, TP offsets/session, fragment metadata, PTB/probe feedback and receiver dispatch.
oracle: Classify the first failed boundary using receiver evidence; do not infer PMTU solely from a lost packet or assume any DPLPMTUD support.
cleanup: Stop fault injection, restore normal communication and verify resource/state recovery before the next case.

diagnostic_steps: Identify transport, TP usage and actual encoded size.
Subtract applicable overhead at each layer.
Compare small and large delivery with receiver/reassembly observations before selecting a cause.

expert_knowledge.summary: Parse SOME/IP message boundaries independently of TCP read and segment boundaries.
expert_knowledge.rationale: TCP does not preserve application write boundaries; parsing and buffering require explicit size and lifecycle handling.
alternatives: Accumulate a bounded header and body before dispatch.
Use an incremental parser with explicit incomplete-message ownership and bounded retention.
failure_modes: One read is treated as one message.
Split headers or multiple messages in one read cause truncation or extra dispatch.
An untrusted length allocates unbounded memory.
srs_guidance: Specify complete-message validation and partial-input handling without assuming TCP segment boundaries.
Keep buffering limits and incomplete-input deadlines as inputs.

cleanup: Stop fault injection, restore normal communication and verify resource/state recovery before the next case.
